adjudication_label: molten salt composition and impurity characterization methods
canonical_question: What specific quantitative composition parameters and impurity levels (e.g., water, oxides) are reported for the molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 salt mixture used in the corrosion study of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy?

question_variants.question: What specific experimental parameters define the composition of the molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 salt mixture?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided text identifies the salt as a 'molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2' mixture but does not specify the stoichiometric ratios, molar fractions, or purity levels that define its exact composition.

answers.answer: The text confirms the use of 'molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl 2 salt' but provides no specific numerical composition parameters (e.g., eutectic ratio, wt%).
answers.boundary_limitation: Composition details (ratios) are not reported in the provided text.
evidence_spans: Here, the molten salt corrosion behavior of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) was evaluated in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl 2 salt at 450 °C and 650 °C in comparison to conventional duplex stainless steel 2205 (DS2205).
The EHEA showed a significantly lower corrosion rate of ~1 mm/year at 450 °C compared to ~8 mm/year for DS2205.
Similarly, EHEA showed a lower corrosion rate of ~9 mm/year at 650 °C compared to ~20 mm/year for DS2205.
